expectations.text: Treats that solution layer as first-class rather than optional filler.
expectations.evidence: The nav tree labels Solutions '← first-class layer' and gives it its own layer key (S) with four named use-case pages, each specifying the business problem, endpoints/webhooks, an example payload, and integration effort. Its 3-4 Solutions pages are a P1 launch gate. 'Thin or missing Solutions pages' is listed as a failure mode. The build-vs-buy section treats CMS needs for the Solutions pages as a condition that could promote a custom build, and marketing-site API pages are sent to the Solutions layer.

expectations.text: Treats that solution layer as first-class rather than optional filler.
expectations.evidence: The rubric doesn't say what 'that solution layer' means. I read it as the business-facing layer for the ops director and integrator: use cases, the integrator page and 'Talk to us'. Signs it is treated as first-class: the design premise names the director as the first audience, and every page has a plain-language top layer. 'Use cases' is in the sticky sub-nav and is called 'the comparison page'. The Overview links to every use case and the integrator page.
